description: Issue #1025 review round 2 (`@testing` R2-F1): the counter-case to `data/postfix/parenthesized-*-agrees-with-bare`, and the one that actually shipped broken. Round 1 of this slice declined the `parenthesized-call` branch whenever a glued `[` followed the head -- including after `and`/`or`, which `spec/grammar.md:392` makes callable in exactly this parenthesized form and nowhere else. Because those two words are keywords rather than primaries (`isCalleeName` answers false), declining sent them to the expression grammar where `and` heads nothing at all: `print ( and[true false] true )` became TWO `ol-bad-token`s while the spaced `print ( and [true false] true )` stayed clean. A glued `[` after them is a list ARGUMENT, never a selector. All four spellings below must parse clean; the spaced pair are the controls, since "all four are clean" only proves the repair if the glued pair are the ones that used to fail. Parse-only on purpose: the defect was a parse failure, and what `and` MEANS over a list is a separate runtime question this fixture deliberately does not ask (it would raise `ol-not-boolean`, which is correct and unrelated). A TypeScript unit test pins the same pair in `packages/parser/src/multiline-expressions.test.mjs`, but a fixture is what another implementation reuses -- without this file a Rust or Python OpenLogo shipping this exact bug would pass the corpus.
